The generated response is refined before delivery, clearly making transmission contingent on human review and allowing edits to alter what the recipient receives. Imago Obscura most closely matches the signature: it operates on the image users intend to share, computes privacy risks, exposes those risks for identification, and lets users mitigate them through image editing before sharing. The assess-then-edit loop plausibly changes disclosure outcomes and generalizes conceptually beyond images. The quote does not explicitly state that sending is technically gated or describe the annotation rendering, so impact and evidence stop short of 5.
